**Synopsis:**
The yen is on track for its best weekly gain since late July, driven by rising BOJ rate hike expectations ahead of its Sept 17–18 meeting, despite pulling back intraday. The dollar is soft broadly, with markets in a holding pattern ahead of US nonfarm payrolls and next week's CPI print. Fed Governor Waller signaled a preference for holding rates steady if inflation continues to moderate, trimming September hike odds back to 50%. Geopolitical risk (US strikes on Iran, elevated Brent >$95) adds an inflation wildcard. JPMorgan flags risk of a sharp yen short squeeze toward 142–146 if BOJ hikes and pension repatriation flows materialize.
